title: Incident update template copy: standard blocks + tone rules + examples per incident phase
creator: Paula Mendes
description:
Goal
Define the canonical customer-facing language blocks for the public status page across incident phases, with:
- A consistent tone (clear, factual, no speculation)
- Fill-in-the-blank structure that scales with component granularity (product x region x capability)
- Examples for common failure modes (streaming-only, embeddings-only, partial region, elevated latency without elevated errors)

This ticket covers copy only (not engineering wiring). Output should be usable in:
- Statuspage incident updates
- Incident-bot drafted updates (templated)
- Console linking surfaces (short summary snippet)

Non-goals
- Defining the component taxonomy (tracked elsewhere)
- Setting hard comms SLAs or promising credits
- Publishing detailed root-cause content beyond the post-incident summary policy

Owners / reviewers
- Owner (copy): Wei Chen
- PM/requirements: Paula Mendes
- Console surface constraints: Marissa Cole
- SRE requirements: Rafael Mendes
- Support alignment: Dev Patel
- Legal review for publishable language: Michael Grant
- Security/compliance review for Dedicated/Private phrasing: Naomi Feldman / Kira Thompson

Acceptance criteria
- Templates for: Investigating, Identified, Mitigating, Monitoring, Resolved, and (link stub) Post-incident summary
- Each template includes: required fields, optional fields, and explicit do/don’t guidance
- Example updates for 3 scenarios:
  1) US-East streaming disconnects (partial impact)
  2) Embeddings elevated 5xx (single capability)
  3) Global elevated latency (degraded performance, no outage)
- Copy works for Hosted API and Dedicated control-plane-visible incidents; includes explicit guidance for Private (often not publicly listed)
- Short summary variant (<= 240 chars) that can be surfaced in Console and/or incident list view

Implementation notes
- Incident-bot will likely populate: component(s), region(s), capability, start time, user impact, workaround/fallback_active, and current mitigation status. Copy must tolerate missing fields early.
- Prefer “Some users” vs “All users” unless confirmed.
- Prefer “elevated error rates/latency” vs “outage” unless we have confirmed unavailability.

=== Canonical tone guide ===
Principles
1) Be specific about what is affected (component + region + capability), even if root cause is unknown.
2) State observable impact (errors, latency, disconnects) and what users should expect.
3) Avoid speculation: no vendor blame, no unverified causal claims, no “we believe” without evidence.
4) Avoid over-promising: no ETAs unless confidence is high and SRE/IC agrees.
5) Avoid sensitive details: no customer names, no capacity shortfalls phrased as “we ran out of GPUs”, no security findings.
6) Prefer active voice and plain language. Keep sentences short.

Words/phrasing constraints
- Use: “degraded performance” for latency regressions or partial failure; “partial outage” for consistent request failures affecting a subset of requests; “major outage” for widespread unavailability.
- Use: “We are investigating” / “We have identified the cause” / “We are mitigating” / “We are monitoring” / “Resolved”.
- Avoid: “unprecedented”, “massive”, “catastrophic”, “should be fixed”, “guarantee”, “no data loss” (unless verified).
- Avoid internal system names (gateway scheduler shard IDs, cluster names). Use public component names.

Update structure (recommended order)
1) What’s impacted (component + region)
2) What users see (symptoms)
3) What we’re doing now (investigating/mitigating)
4) Workarounds (if any)
5) Next update expectation (time window) — optional; never a hard promise


=== Status update templates ===

[1] INVESTIGATING (Initial update)
When to use
- Incident declared, impact is plausible/confirmed, cause unknown.

Required fields
- Affected component(s)
- Region(s)
- Customer-facing symptom (errors/latency/disconnects)
- Start time window (“since HH:MM UTC”)
- Commitment to next update window (broad)

Template (long)
"We are investigating an issue affecting {component} in {region}. Some users may experience {symptom}. We have been observing this since {time_utc}. We’ll share another update within {next_update_window}."

Template (short, <=240 chars)
"Investigating: {component} ({region}) – {symptom}. Observed since {time_utc}. Next update in {next_update_window}."

Do / Don’t
- Do: say “some users” until scope is measured.
- Don’t: speculate on root cause (“provider networking”, “capacity exhaustion”) unless confirmed and approved.


[2] IDENTIFIED
When to use
- We have a clear root cause class (not necessarily full RCA), or confirmed trigger.

Required fields
- What changed / what failed (generic, non-sensitive)
- Current impact state (ongoing vs improving)

Template (long)
"We’ve identified the cause of the issue affecting {component} in {region} as {cause_class}. Users may still see {symptom}. We are working on {mitigation_action} and will provide another update within {next_update_window}."

Template (short)
"Identified: {component} ({region}) – {cause_class}. Mitigation in progress; {symptom} may persist. Next update in {next_update_window}."

Cause class examples (approved vocabulary)
- “a configuration change”
- “a dependency degradation”
- “increased load leading to saturation” (only if approved; avoid implying capacity mismanagement)
- “a software regression in the serving path”
- “a networking issue impacting connectivity”


[3] MITIGATING
When to use
- Active mitigation is underway (rollback, failover, routing change, rate limiting, patch deploy).

Required fields
- Mitigation steps (safe, non-sensitive)
- What users should expect (improving vs intermittent)

Template (long)
"We are actively mitigating the issue affecting {component} in {region} by {mitigation_action}. Some users may continue to experience {symptom}. We’ll continue to monitor and share another update within {next_update_window}."

Template (short)
"Mitigating: {component} ({region}) – applying {mitigation_action}. {symptom} may continue. Next update in {next_update_window}."

Optional additions
- Workaround: “If possible, retry failed requests” or “Consider switching regions if your configuration supports it.” (Only if true for typical customers; avoid instructions that don’t exist.)
- Fallback: “We have enabled fallback to a compatible model variant for some traffic.” (Only if this is accurate + approved by IC.)


[4] MONITORING
When to use
- Metrics indicate recovery; we’re watching to ensure stability.

Required fields
- Current state: improving/mostly recovered
- Monitoring window before resolve (optional)

Template (long)
"Mitigation is in place and we are seeing recovery for {component} in {region}. Some users may still experience intermittent {symptom}. We are monitoring closely and will confirm full resolution once metrics remain stable."

Template (short)
"Monitoring: recovery observed for {component} ({region}). Intermittent {symptom} may persist while we monitor stability."


[5] RESOLVED
When to use
- Customer-facing metrics stable; incident closed.

Required fields
- End time
- High-level fix summary (non-sensitive)
- Post-incident summary link expectation (per policy)

Template (long)
"This incident has been resolved for {component} in {region}. Impact occurred from {impact_start_utc} to {impact_end_utc} and users may have experienced {symptom}. The issue was resolved by {resolution_action}. We will publish a post-incident summary within {summary_timeline} as outlined in our incident communications policy."

Template (short)
"Resolved: {component} ({region}) – impact {impact_start_utc}–{impact_end_utc}. {resolution_action}. Post-incident summary to follow."

Notes
- "summary_timeline" should match PM-612 policy; if policy differs by severity, keep it generic (e.g., “as soon as available”).


[6] POST-INCIDENT SUMMARY (link stub copy)
Used on incident timeline once summary is published
"Post-incident summary: {summary_link}"
Console snippet variant
"Read the post-incident summary: {summary_link}"


=== Guidance for Dedicated / Private messaging ===
Dedicated
- If there is a public component representing a Dedicated control plane surface area, we can post updates that describe the platform impact without naming tenants.
- Avoid: “Customer X impacted”, “single-tenant cluster issue”, “hardware shortfall on reserved capacity.”
- Prefer: “a subset of Dedicated deployments in {region}” if and only if that scope is approved and does not imply customer identity.

Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Default: do not post on public status page unless it affects shared/control plane surfaces that are publicly represented.
- If asked, redirect to Support/CS channels per escalation playbook; do not imply broader impact.


=== Examples ===

Example A: Partial streaming degradation (US-East)
Investigating (long)
"We are investigating an issue affecting Hosted API Streaming in us-east. Some users may experience streaming disconnects or delayed tokens. We have been observing this since 14:07 UTC. We’ll share another update within 30 minutes."
Identified (long)
"We’ve identified the cause of the issue affecting Hosted API Streaming in us-east as a regression in our streaming connection handling. Users may still see intermittent disconnects. We are rolling back the change and will provide another update within 30 minutes."
Monitoring (long)
"Mitigation is in place and we are seeing recovery for Hosted API Streaming in us-east. Some users may still experience intermittent disconnects while we monitor stability."
Resolved (long)
"This incident has been resolved for Hosted API Streaming in us-east. Impact occurred from 14:07 to 15:02 UTC and users may have experienced streaming disconnects or delayed tokens. The issue was resolved by rolling back a recent change. A post-incident summary will be published as soon as available."

Example B: Embeddings elevated 5xx (EU-West)
Investigating (short)
"Investigating: Embeddings (eu-west) – elevated 5xx errors. Observed since 09:41 UTC. Next update in 30 minutes."
Mitigating (long)
"We are actively mitigating the issue affecting Embeddings in eu-west by shifting traffic and restarting affected workers. Some users may continue to see elevated 5xx errors. We’ll continue to monitor and share another update within 30 minutes."

Example C: Global degraded performance (latency)
Investigating (long)
"We are investigating degraded performance affecting Hosted API Requests in multiple regions. Some users may experience elevated latency. We have been observing this since 18:22 UTC. We’ll share another update within 30 minutes."
Identified (long)
"We’ve identified the cause of the degraded performance as a dependency degradation affecting request processing. Users may continue to see elevated latency while we apply mitigation. We will provide another update within 30 minutes."


=== Open questions / follow-ups ===
- Confirm whether we want “Next update within X minutes” always present vs optional for lower severity. Current recommendation: required for Investigating/Identified/Mitigating; optional for Monitoring/Resolved.
- Confirm the default “summary_timeline” wording to match PM-612 without creating a hard promise.
- Confirm allowed workaround language about “switch regions” (depends on customer configuration and product docs).

Deliverables
- Final copy blocks to be pasted into Confluence incident templates doc + provided to ENG-4822 for incident-bot templating.
- Short snippets for incident list/Console surfaces.
comments: 2025-11-08 (Paula Mendes): Creating this ticket after the copy review feedback in DES-244. We need canonical wording before ENG-4822 locks templates in incident-bot. Please keep early-phase language conservative and avoid ETAs unless we can make it conditional ("within X minutes" ok; "resolved by" not ok).

2025-11-09 (Wei Chen): Drafting initial set of blocks. Question: do we want to say “partial outage” vs “degraded performance” when errors are high but not 100%? Proposal: “partial outage” only when failure rate is sustained and >~25% of requests for the component, otherwise “degraded performance” with symptom spelled out.

2025-11-10 (Rafael Mendes): +1. Also please ensure the templates support multi-component incidents (e.g., Streaming + Chat) without becoming unreadable. Maybe recommend 1–2 top impacted components for public status, with more detail in summary.

2025-11-12 (Dev Patel): Support ask: please add a standard sentence we can reuse in replies when customers dispute accuracy (e.g., “Status reflects aggregate platform health for the listed components”). Not necessarily for status page itself, but we need alignment in tone.

2025-11-13 (Marissa Cole): For Console linking, we need a short summary that can fit in a card. Please provide a <=240 char version per state and avoid using “Hosted API” repeatedly (we can prefix with product context in UI).

2025-11-15 (Michael Grant): Legal review notes: avoid “no data loss” language and avoid implying customer-specific impact. "Dependency degradation" is ok; naming specific vendors is not. "Increased load leading to saturation" is ok only if it doesn’t imply we failed to plan capacity; prefer "traffic spike" + "protective measures" phrasing.

2025-11-18 (Naomi Feldman): For Dedicated/Private, keep language generic and do not confirm whether a specific tenant is impacted. Recommend adding explicit guidance: Private incidents typically handled via direct customer channels unless shared control plane is impacted.
2025-11-20 (Wei Chen): Incorporated feedback; added approved vocabulary list and Dedicated/Private guidance. Added 3 example scenarios. Marking ready for final review.
2025-11-22 (Paula Mendes): Approved. Please sync final blocks to Confluence incident templates and ping Devon (ENG-4822) to match bot templates. Marking Done.
final_artifacts: Copy blocks for Investigating/Identified/Mitigating/Monitoring/Resolved + post-incident summary link stub
Three scenario examples (streaming partial impact, embeddings 5xx, global latency)
Short summary variants for Console/incident list surfaces
handoff_notes_for_engineering: ENG-4822: You can treat the quoted templates as canonical. Fields expected for substitution: {component}, {region}, {symptom}, {time_utc}, {next_update_window}, {cause_class}, {mitigation_action}, {impact_start_utc}, {impact_end_utc}, {resolution_action}, {summary_timeline}, {summary_link}. Templates must tolerate missing optional fields (omit sentences rather than leaving placeholders). Keep “some users” default unless incident intake explicitly sets scope=all.
risk_notes: Main risk is over-specific language early in incident lifecycle. Templates intentionally avoid ETAs and avoid sensitive operational details (vendor names, customer-specific capacity constraints).
